title: Retention Settings in Console — IA, warnings, and permissions model
creator: Tessa Morgan
description:
Goal
Design the Redwood Console “Retention Settings” experience for admins across Hosted/Dedicated/Private tenants, with clear information architecture, warning states, and a permissions model that matches security/compliance expectations.

Context / Why
Retention controls are a procurement blocker for regulated customers (Dedicated/Private). The console needs to make retention policy behavior explicit (TTL + purge semantics + exceptions like legal hold), reduce misconfiguration, and support evidence generation (downloadable exports) without turning this into a full GRC tool.

Primary personas
- Security Admin: configures retention to match policy; needs auditability and exports.
- SRE/Platform Admin: cares about operational debugging needs; wants safe defaults and guardrails.
- Auditor (read-only): views policy + change history; downloads export for evidence packet.

Scope for this ticket (Design)
1) Information architecture
- Location: Console → Settings → Security & Compliance → Retention
- Page sections (top to bottom):
  A. Summary banner (current effective policy, tier defaults, last updated, legal hold status)
  B. Data classes table (editable where supported)
  C. Advanced settings (region scope + overrides if enabled, export/download, change history)
  D. Help + docs links + “Request Compliance Report Pack” CTA (gated by role)

2) Data classes UI model
Each row represents a data class with consistent controls:
- Data class name + short description
- Storage scope indicator: Control plane / Data plane / Third-party (where relevant)
- Retention control: TTL selector (days) with min/max constraints by tier
- Status pill: “Default”, “Customized”, “Not collected”, “Locked (Legal hold)”, “Not supported in this deployment”
- “Details” drawer: purge semantics, what gets deleted, timing expectations, and known exceptions

In-scope data classes for v1 UI
- Request/response logs (where enabled)
- Prompts/completions (only if stored; reflect logging mode)
- Audit logs
- Traces
- Metrics
- Artifacts (eval datasets / uploaded artifacts) — display-only if not yet enforceable

3) Warning states + guardrails
Global warnings (top banner)
- Legal hold active: “Retention is currently overridden by an active hold. Editing is disabled for affected data classes.” Includes link to view hold details and the approval workflow note.
- Policy drift / enforcement lag: if verification signals show high TTL lag or purge failures (read-only indicator; links to dashboards).
- Deployment limitations: show when certain classes are not enforceable in a given deployment mode.

Inline warnings (per row / per field)
- Below default retention: warning copy that shortened retention may impact debugging/incident response; require confirmation.
- Below minimum TTL: hard validation error (cannot save).
- Disabled logging mode: if request logs are disabled, show “Not collected” and hide TTL control; show link to logging settings.
- Changing audit log retention: extra warning + “Recommended minimum” copy; require second confirmation.

Save flow / confirmations
- Draft changes tracked on page; “Review changes” modal lists diffs by data class.
- Confirmations:
  - Any decrease in retention requires typed confirmation (string: DELETE) for users without “Break-glass” role.
  - For “Security Admin” role: regular confirmation.
  - For “SRE Break-glass” role: additional note that change is logged and time-bounded access is required.

4) Permissions model (RBAC)
Read-only roles
- Auditor: view effective policy + change history + export current configuration.
- Support/Read-only: view only (no export if customer chooses to restrict).

Write roles
- Security Admin: edit TTL values within allowed bounds; cannot override legal hold; can download exports.
- Org Owner: same as Security Admin + can delegate permissions.

Break-glass / exception capability (separate permission)
- “Retention.Override” capability: allowed to temporarily increase retention during incident response (if configured), but cannot reduce below minimums.
- UI requirement: show “Break-glass required” chip and route to existing access request flow; all actions must generate an audit log event.

Export/report permissions
- “Retention.Export” capability: can download retention configuration export.
- “CompliancePack.Request” capability: can trigger compliance report pack generation/request flow (MVP is request ticket creation / async job; see ENG follow-up).

5) Change history + auditability (UI expectations)
- Read-only “Change history” table on the page:
  - Timestamp, actor, data classes affected, old TTL → new TTL, reason (optional field), source (Console/API/Terraform)
- Provide “Copy JSON” action for the effective policy (for security questionnaire responses).

Design deliverables
- Figma: page layout + empty/loaded/error states
- Component specs for: data class table rows, diff modal, legal hold lock state, permission-gated actions
- Copy deck: warning copy + helper text + tooltips reviewed by Security/GRC

Acceptance criteria
- IA aligns with Console nav conventions and doesn’t add new top-level sections.
- Clear, non-ambiguous labels differentiating “Not collected” vs “Retained for X days”.
- Warning states cover: disabled logging, min/max TTL validation, legal hold lock, enforcement lag indicator.
- Permissions map to capabilities; no “silent” hidden failures (users see why actions are disabled).
- Export actions are discoverable but not noisy; can be performed by Auditor/Security Admin.

Open questions (captured for Eng/PM)
- Per-region overrides: do we expose in v1 or keep as read-only indicator (ADR suggests evaluation in control plane; UI can support later)?
- Enforcement timing language: how specific can we be (“within 24h” vs “best effort”) without creating an SLA?
- Artifacts retention: do we ship as display-only row with “Coming soon” or omit entirely from v1?

Links / references
- Confluence (UX spec target): sources/confluence/product-docs/design-specs/console-retention-settings-page-spec.json
- PRD: sources/confluence/product-docs/requirements/retention-controls-prd.json
- Legal hold policy: sources/confluence/security-and-compliance/data-residency-and-retention/legal-hold-and-retention-exceptions.json
- FAQ inputs (copy alignment): sources/confluence/sales-enablement/security-faq/retention-controls-and-compliance-reporting-faq.json

Handoff notes
- Please ensure backend exposes enough metadata for the UI pills: “not collected”, “not supported”, “locked by hold”, and min/max TTL bounds.
- Console should request “effective policy” (post-evaluation) plus “configured policy” (what the admin set) to avoid confusion when defaults/overrides apply.

Follow-ups (new tickets suggested)
- Console: enforcement verification indicator wiring + dashboard deep links (ENG + SRE)
- Console: request compliance pack CTA flow (async job/request + status)
- Console: per-region override editor (Phase 2+) if product confirms requirement
comments: 2025-01-24 (Naomi Feldman): Please make sure we distinguish audit logs vs request logs clearly. Audit logs retention is a hard procurement item; we need conservative copy and a recommended minimum callout.
2025-01-27 (Marcus Lin): +1 on conservative defaults. Also, legal hold state must fully lock editing for affected stores. We need explicit UI that the hold overrides customer TTL and is audited.

2025-01-29 (Sean Gallagher): Avoid UI that encourages ultra-short retention (<7d) for request logs without warning. On-call needs enough context; propose ‘Below default’ warning + typed confirmation for decreases.

2025-02-03 (Ethan Park): From control plane POV we can return both configured and effective policy + per-class min/max. Per-region overrides exist in schema but we’d prefer read-only in v1 UI to reduce complexity.
2025-02-06 (Olga Petrov): Auditor persona needs export + screenshotable change history. Make sure copy says export is ‘configuration snapshot’ and include last-updated timestamp.
2025-02-10 (Tessa Morgan): Updated spec to include explicit pills: Not collected vs Not supported. Added ‘Review changes’ diff modal and separate permissions for Export + Compliance Pack request.
